title: Weather, Not Climate
subtitle: Emotional context dynamics in transformer KV-cache geometry: dose-dependent drift (the contrast and scar results are withdrawn)
abstract: These experiments do not answer whether an emotion signal in KV keys accumulates across conversation turns; the dose-response experiment cannot test it, because its compared arms differ in text at every read site (the single-turn result this builds on was corrected in October 2026: a story-emotion decode from KV keys at 12.3x chance (40.9%), not W_K and not user state. It is not significantly above a text (TF-IDF) baseline (re-run at 0.410 (369/900, one trial from May's 368) vs 0.370, 5-fold, Holm p = 0.071), and its margin depends on a residualization fitted on each test fold (0.348, exploratory, when fitted on the training fold). The described method is not above text (TF-IDF): 0.358 vs 0.382, 10-fold. On a binary split of ten emotions (not a valence axis), AUROC 0.992 beats untuned text (TF-IDF; Holm p = 0.006; DeLong, trials treated as independent; test-fold FWL; no tuned baseline) but is n=300 and arousal-confounded). The pooled gap between scripted cheerful and hostile conversations shows no monotone trend as their dose grows (0.53, 0.72, 0.53 and 0.78 at doses 1, 2, 4 and 8; per topic it grows in one, shrinks in another and is near zero at dose 1 in the third once one rerun encoded short is left out; three topics; read over equal-width chunks that mix user, assistant and probe tokens, not the user's own tokens), while the readings drift with dose and sequence position. The contrast-overshoot and uncertainty-scar results are withdrawn (November 2026): at the measured turn the compared arms were sent different user messages, and every other comparison between Experiment 2's arms is withdrawn with them.
